verdict.rationale: Appwrite's database docs say its managed database APIs come "with permissions," which is a first-party access-control capability for data. The pack never documents how these permissions work or whether they can restrict rows per user. missing for 10: documentation of per-user or per-row permission rules, examples of configuring row-level access, details of how permissions are enforced, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can restrict data access per user with row-level security policies or security rules

citations.quote: from managed APIs with permissions and realtime to dedicated native engines you connect to directly
